source: Aggarwal et al. (2023) Let's Sample Step by Step: Adaptive-Consistency
finding: First LLM paper to stop sampling early with a Bayesian Beta stopping rule on the vote counts. It stops when the posterior chance that the leading answer is the true mode passes a threshold.
numbers: 17 reasoning and code datasets, up to 40 samples (50-100 for code). Sample budget cut by up to 7.9x with average accuracy drop under 0.1%.
limits: Threshold (95% default) is a free parameter. Assumes samples are exchangeable draws.
agent_relevance: This is the 'stop after enough agreement' rule for the S0 gate and stop rule. Beta is about 4 orders of magnitude faster than the Dirichlet or CRP variants.

source: Aggarwal et al. (2023) Adaptive-Consistency, results by model and task family
finding: Savings hold across model sizes but are smaller for weaker models.
numbers: Sample reduction: GPT-3.5-Turbo 4.4x, Vicuna-13B 1.9x, Code-davinci-002 3.4x (accuracy delta +0.0). By family: math 3.3x fewer samples (-0.1% acc), commonsense 2.9x (-0.2%), symbolic 3.8x (no loss), coding 2.4x (+0.4%).
limits: The weaker model reaches consensus less early, so savings fall to 1.9x.
agent_relevance: Expect the saving to grow with model strength and shrink with answer-space size. Measure it, do not assume it.

source: Aggarwal et al. (2023) Adaptive-Consistency, equal-cost comparison and stopping functions
finding: At equal average sample cost, adaptive stopping beats fixed-budget self-consistency. Six stopping functions were compared: RANDOM, MAJORITY, ENTROPY, BETA, DIRICHLET, CRP.
numbers: GSM8K: at average cost 10 samples, about 3% higher accuracy than fixed k=10. SVAMP: comparable accuracy with under 5 samples on average. Boolean Expressions: 7.9x budget cut, no loss. BETA beats ENTROPY, which beats MAJORITY; RANDOM is worst; DIRICHLET and CRP match BETA but are about 4 orders of magnitude slower.
limits: Gains are largest when a majority is clear early or the answer set is small. The paper's limitation note: model biases persist, since a consensus can be consistently wrong.
agent_relevance: A plain 'majority above a threshold' rule is the weakest informed rule. Prefer a posterior or sequential test.

source: Li et al. (2024, ICLR) Escape Sky-high Cost: Early-Stopping Self-Consistency (ESC)
finding: Split the sample budget into small windows (size 5; 8 for MATH). Stop at the first window where all answers agree (zero entropy). No posterior needed.
numbers: Average samples cut: MATH -33.8%, GSM8K -80.1%, StrategyQA -76.8%, CommonsenseQA -78.5%, Coin Flip -84.2%, Last Letters -67.4%, with comparable accuracy. Averaged over 10 runs, three models (GPT-4, GPT-3.5-Turbo, Llama-2-7b). Plain SC given the same average sample count loses accuracy along the normal SC curve.
limits: Hard tasks (MATH) save least. Window size is tuned per task. Coin Flip on GPT-4 is already 100%, so it was skipped.
agent_relevance: A fixed rule 'stop when a window of 5 samples all agree' is the simple baseline that the SUBFIELDS note asks about. Easy to put in a scaffold.

source: Li et al. (2024) ESC control scheme
finding: Derives a z-statistic estimate from the first observation window to choose window size w and max size L for a target performance-cost balance. A uniform window is treated as a Bernoulli event under a null on the modal answer's probability.
numbers: Algorithm 2 uses an initial window of 5 across the dataset, then predicts expected accuracy loss and sample count for each (w, L).
limits: Estimate relies on first-window frequencies, which are noisy for small windows.
agent_relevance: Gives a way to set the stop rule per task from a pilot batch, not by hand.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Make Every Penny Count: Difficulty-Adaptive Self-Consistency (DSC)
finding: Adds prior difficulty information: rank questions by difficulty, give easy ones a single CoT sample, pre-allocate sample size for hard ones. Counts input cost as well as output cost.
numbers: Cost vs fixed SC: -65.29% on GPT-4, -56.04% on GPT-3.5-Turbo. Versus ESC (best baseline): -24.81% GPT-4, -21.86% GPT-3.5-Turbo. Six benchmarks. On GSM8K, CoT and SC (40 samples) give the same answer on 96.2% of items for GPT-4 and 84.8% for GPT-3.5-Turbo.
limits: Needs a batch of queries for difficulty ranking, and the ranking costs LLM calls. Input tokens (few-shot prompts) can outweigh output savings.
agent_relevance: A one-sample-first gate (S0) is justified: for strong models most items need no voting. Count prompt tokens when costing a resample.

source: Wan et al. (2025) Reasoning Aware Self-Consistency (RASC)
finding: Scores each sample on answer consistency and rationale quality, stops on criteria over these scores, and weights the vote by rationale fidelity.
numbers: Sample usage cut by about 70% (60-80% range) with accuracy kept, across QA datasets. Also improves faithfulness of the chosen rationale.
limits: Needs an extra scoring pass per sample and relies on the model grading its own reasoning.
agent_relevance: Stop evidence can include reasoning quality, not only answer counts.

source: Lee et al. (2025) ConSol: Sequential Probability Ratio Testing to Find Consistent LLM Reasoning Paths Efficiently
finding: First direct use of Wald's SPRT (and a mixture SPRT) to stop self-consistency sampling. It tests whether the top answer's share is above 0.5. They set p1=0.5001 (usual 0.55-0.6) to detect small margins.
numbers: Token reduction vs SC@40: SPRT 63.9% (AIME24 o3-mini-low), 84.8% (o3-mini-medium), 84.5% (high), 86.2% (GPQA Diamond o3-mini-low), 88.6% (GSM gpt-4o-mini); mSPRT 57.3-88.7%. Adaptive-Consistency 47.9-82.8%; p-value rule 49.3-79.2%. Accuracy: AIME24 low 80.0% SPRT vs 70.0% SC@40; GSM 93.5% vs 94.2%; GPQA 66.7% vs 68.2%.
limits: SPRT could sample past 40, which partly explains the AIME24 low gain (70 to 80%, 30 problems, so 3 items). Only short-answer and multiple-choice tasks. Small N on AIME24.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that a classical Wald test saves 55-89% of tokens at near-equal accuracy. Best single fit for our stop rule.

source: Lee et al. (2025) ConSol, calibration details
finding: Treats the answer as top-answer vs others (Bernoulli), as Adaptive-Consistency did when it reduced Dirichlet to Beta. The mixture SPRT puts a truncated Beta prior on p in (0.5,1]. Textbook SPRT settings were too insensitive to a close second answer.
numbers: Confidence setting about 0.94998 for SPRT and 0.94994 for mSPRT. Sampling 2-3 responses in parallel per turn cuts latency at some cost to savings.
limits: The authors name parameter sensitivity as the main limit and leave systematic calibration to future work.
agent_relevance: Textbook thresholds do not transfer to LLM voting. Calibrate on logged attempts.

source: Taubenfeld et al. (2025) Confidence Improves Self-Consistency in LLMs (CISC)
finding: Weights each vote by the model's own confidence (P(True) works best). Not a stop rule, but it reaches the same accuracy with fewer samples, which moves the stop point earlier.
numbers: Nine models, four datasets (MMLU, MATH, GSM8K, BBH): over 40% fewer reasoning paths on average. P(True): 41% cost reduction at budget 5, 46% at budget 10. SC needs 18.6 samples to match CISC with 10. Gemma2-9B on MATH: 73% cost reduction.
limits: Gains vary by model and dataset; some cells show no saving. Needs a confidence call per sample.
agent_relevance: Combine count-based stopping with confidence-weighted votes. Within-question confidence is what matters, not cross-question calibration.

source: Fu et al. (2025) Deep Think with Confidence (DeepConf)
finding: Online mode stops weak traces when group confidence falls below a warmup threshold, and stops the whole job once the top answer's vote share passes a consensus threshold tau.
numbers: Models: DeepSeek-8B, Qwen3-8B/32B, GPT-OSS-20B/120B; AIME24/25, HMMT25, BRUMO25, GPQA-Diamond; 64 repetitions. DeepConf@512 reaches 99.9% on AIME25 (GPT-OSS-120B) vs 97.0% for cons@512 and 91.8% pass@1. Token cut vs majority vote: DeepConf-low 43-79% (mean 62.88%), DeepConf-high 18-59% (mean 47.67%); up to 84.7% overall.
limits: DeepConf-low loses accuracy in some settings (Qwen3-32B BRUMO25 -0.9pp; GPT-OSS-120B HMMT25). Needs token log-probs and 16 warmup traces.
agent_relevance: Two-level stopping: kill bad paths early and stop the vote when consensus is high.

source: Fu et al. (2025) DeepConf, consensus-threshold ablation
finding: More aggressive consensus thresholds save more but begin to cost accuracy.
numbers: tau 0.95: DeepConf-low saves 15.4% / 52.8% of tokens at B=32 / 512, DeepConf-high 22.0% / 54.7%, accuracy unchanged. tau 0.90 and 0.85 raise savings up to 69.6% but accuracy drops (-0.26pp at 0.90 for DeepConf-low). tau 1.0 weakens savings with no accuracy gain.
limits: Ablation on one benchmark (AIME24).
agent_relevance: A stop threshold has a knee near 0.95 consensus. Verify on logged runs.

source: Zhu et al. (2025) Path-Consistency with Prefix Enhancement
finding: Uses the most confident earlier answer's prefix to guide later branches, cutting tokens spent on random samples.
numbers: Ten datasets. Average speedup: math 28.7%, commonsense 20.9%, symbolic 20.3%; up to 28.9% (GSM8K), 48.3%, 42.0%, 42.7% on other math sets; accuracy gains up to 3.8% (SVAMP).
limits: Gains are smaller than pure early stopping; the method is meant to combine with it.
agent_relevance: Feeding a partial result forward is an alternative to restarting each attempt from scratch.

source: Huang et al. (2025) Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Self-Calibration
finding: Distils self-consistency into the model so its confidence is calibrated, then uses it for early-stopping Best-of-N and confidence-weighted voting.
numbers: Confidence-weighted SC reaches accuracy 85.0 with 94.2% fewer samples than standard SC on the plotted setting. MathQA accuracy 81.0 to 83.6 at an average of 16 responses. Other points on the curve save 50.4% and 39.8%.
limits: Needs training to calibrate, so it is not scaffold-only. Raw LLM confidence is overconfident.
agent_relevance: Without training, raw self-confidence is a weak stop signal. Use agreement counts.

source: Yang et al. (2025) Dynamic Early Exit in Reasoning Models (DEER)
finding: At reasoning transition words, prompts the model for a trial answer and stops thinking when the trial answer's confidence is high. Training-free.
numbers: 11 reasoning models, 10 benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH-500, AMC, GPQA, AIME, LiveCodeBench). CoT length cut by 19.1% to 80.1% on average, accuracy up 0.3% to 5.0%.
limits: Sensitive to the answer-inducing prompt; the DEER-Pro variant runs parallel answer inductions to be robust. Savings range is wide across models.
agent_relevance: A within-trajectory stop test: probe for an answer at step boundaries and stop when it is stable and confident.

source: Liu and Wang (2025) Answer Convergence as a Signal for Early Stopping in Reasoning
finding: On math, models typically reach their final answer after about 60% of the reasoning steps. Three methods: early stop on answer consistency across successive prefixes, boosting end-of-thinking probability, and a supervised Learn-to-Stop probe on activations.
numbers: Five benchmarks, five open-weight LLMs. Answer-consistency stopping cuts tokens by over 40% on NaturalQuestions and raises accuracy. Learn-to-Stop cuts up to 48% of tokens on NQ with QwQ-32B.
limits: Unsupervised rules work well on simple datasets only; the supervised probe kept accuracy on both simple and complex tasks.
agent_relevance: Same limit as sampling stops: easy items stop safely, hard items need a stronger signal.

source: Kalayci and Raman (2025) Optimal Stopping vs Best-of-N for Inference Time Optimization
finding: Casts repeated generation as Pandora's Box: each sample costs something and has a random reward. A UCB-style algorithm learns stopping thresholds on the fly with regret close to Weitzman's optimal rule.
numbers: On AlpacaFarm and HH-RLHF with several LLM and reward-model pairs: same quality as non-adaptive Best-of-N with 15-35% fewer generations on average; savings grow from 15% to 35% as the quality target rises.
limits: Needs a scalar reward model. Not applicable where there is no scorer or verifier.
agent_relevance: Gives the 'value of one more attempt' framing from the SUBFIELDS note, with a regret guarantee, when a scorer exists.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
finding: Coverage (fraction of problems solved by any sample) grows log-linearly over four orders of magnitude of samples and fits an exponentiated power law. Without a verifier, majority voting and reward models plateau.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite with DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct: 15.9% with 1 sample to 56% with 250 samples (single-sample SOTA 43%). Majority vote and reward-model selection plateau beyond several hundred samples.
limits: Large gains need an automatic verifier; selection without one is the bottleneck.
agent_relevance: Agreement-based stopping is only safe if errors are not correlated. With a verifier, stop at the first verified pass instead of voting.

source: Wang et al. (2023, ICLR) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning
finding: The fixed-budget baseline (40 samples, majority vote) that all the stopping work above is compared against.
numbers: Gains over greedy CoT: GSM8K +17.9%, SVAMP +11.0%, AQuA +12.2% (abstract).
limits: Fixed k for every question, no stop rule. Gains saturate as k grows.
agent_relevance: Reference cost the sequential rules try to beat.

source: Wald (1945) Sequential Tests of Statistical Hypotheses; Wald (1947) Sequential Analysis
finding: Founding work: draw observations one at a time, compute the likelihood ratio, stop when it crosses an upper or lower boundary set by the allowed error rates (about A=(1-beta)/alpha, B=beta/(1-alpha)).
numbers: From memory, not verified: needs on average about half the observations of the best fixed-sample test at the same error rates (Wald-Wolfowitz 1948 optimality).
limits: [M] memory only. ConSol (c08) restates the SPRT setup and cites Wald 1945.
agent_relevance: Base of the stop rule. Treat as unverified until the paper is opened.

source: Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe and Sekhon (2022) Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences
finding: Confidence sequences stay valid at any stopping time. The paper links the SPRT, Cramer-Chernoff bounds and the law of the iterated logarithm.
numbers: Abstract and intro read. No LLM numbers.
limits: Theory paper. Included for the statistics: peeking at a fixed-sample test inflates error.
agent_relevance: An LLM loop that checks agreement after every sample is peeking. Time-uniform bounds are the formal fix.

source: Ramdas, Grunwald, Vovk and Shafer (2023) Game-Theoretic Statistics and Safe Anytime-Valid Inference
finding: Safe anytime-valid inference: e-processes and confidence sequences stay valid under optional stopping or continuation for any reason, via test martingales and Ville's inequality.
numbers: Abstract and intro read. No numbers.
limits: Survey; no LLM experiments. Needs a well-defined null for LLM sample answers.
agent_relevance: Candidate formal stop rule that stays valid however often the agent looks.

source: Johari, Pekelis and Walsh (2019) Always Valid Inference: Continuous Monitoring of A/B Tests
finding: Only the title and first lines were seen. Claim from title: continuous peeking at p-values inflates false positives and always-valid p-values fix it.
numbers: None recorded.
limits: Not read beyond the header.
agent_relevance: Same concern as c21 and c22.

source: Synthesis of early-stop rules in LLM sampling (c01-c19)
finding: Across Adaptive-Consistency, ESC, ConSol, DSC, DeepConf and RASC, savings are 2x to 8x in samples with under 1 point accuracy loss on math, QA and commonsense. Savings are largest on easy or small-answer-set tasks and smallest on hard ones (ESC: MATH -33.8% vs GSM8K -80.1%).
numbers: Token savings: ConSol SPRT 64-89%, ESC 34-84%, Adaptive-Consistency 2-8x, DeepConf-low mean 62.9%, DSC 56-65% of cost, CISC over 40% of paths, Pandora UCB 15-35%.
limits: Baselines (SC@40, SC@512, Best-of-N) and cost units (samples, tokens, dollars) differ, so figures are not comparable. Nearly all tests use short-answer tasks.
agent_relevance: Use a sequential test on the top answer's share, gate with one cheap sample first, and calibrate the threshold on logged attempts.

source: Gap note on LLM sequential-stopping evidence (c01-c24)
url: (no single source; assessed from the papers read)
finding: No paper found in this pass tests stopping for open-ended generation, multi-step agent tasks, or correlated model errors. No failed replications of the stop rules were found; ConSol reports parameter sensitivity and DeepConf reports accuracy drops at aggressive thresholds.
numbers: None. Search was limited: WebSearch quota was exhausted and the OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs returned rate-limit errors, so only papers with known arXiv ids were fetched.
limits: 2025-2026 coverage is incomplete.
agent_relevance: Open test: does a posterior or SPRT stop beat the fixed-window rule on logged attempts at equal tokens.
